To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thresholding estimation and 1 penalized estimation of large covariance, correlation and precision matrices can be applied to temporally dependent data, and a gapblock cross validation is proposed for tuning parameter selection.

the thresholding estimation of large covariance matrix, the 1 minimization estimation of precision matrix and the gapblock cross validation are applicable to high dimensional temporally dependent data with slowly decaying long range dependence.
several commonly used estimation methods for large covariance and precision matrix can be applied to temporally dependent data, with the same convergence rates as in the independent case.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new problem of estimating the covariance and precision matrices of high dimensional data when they are temporally dependent, and provides some new results on the estimation of the covariance and correlation matrices.
the estimation and prediction of large covariance and correlation matrices from temporally dependent data with slowly decaying memory.
the estimation of large dimensional covariance, correlation and precision matrices from temporally dependent high dimensional data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results in this paper are very important for the estimation of large precision matrices and covariance matrices.

we can use all the existing methods for the estimation of large correlation and covariance matrices from independent data for the estimation of these matrices from temporally dependent data as long as the temporal dependence is short ranged.
the methods developed in this paper are applicable to the temporally correlated observations, and can be used in a wide range of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can apply several commonly used methods in the literature for independent data to the temporally correlated data.

the commonly used methods for estimating covariance or precision matrices from independent observations can be directly applied to temporally dependent observations, and the rates of convergence and sparsistency can be established under the slowly decaying temporal dependency.
the temporal dependence in data does not affect the estimation accuracy of covariance and precision matrices as long as the memory parameter is smaller than one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the commonly used methods for estimating covariance and correlation matrices can be directly applied to temporally dependent data without the need for additional modifications.
the existing methods for high dimensional independent data can be extended to temporally dependent data with slowly decaying dependence.

the commonly used methods for estimating large covariance and precision matrix from independent data can be applied to temporally dependent data as well, and the resulting estimators have the same convergence rate as the estimators based on independent data.
